gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: He lowered his voice ___ wake the baby.
gaps.explanation: Negative purpose = so as not to / in order not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: ___ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite' is followed by a noun or -ing form, never a finite clause.
'Due to personal reasons' is the standard collocation for giving a cause.

gaps.sentence: He didn't whisper the news; ___, he announced it to the whole office.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' corrects the first statement with its opposite.

gaps.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if/though + past' describes behaviour contrary to fact (he doesn't own it).
'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.

gaps.sentence: The expedition will go ahead ___ the sponsors confirm the funding.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' = only if, a formal positive condition.
